reading_note: The teaching describes the ascent of divine good-and-truth (light) from its captivity in the natural mind, through successive boundaries between discrete degrees (firmaments), back toward its celestial source. The arc: a question is raised whether any living truth comes forth from the threefold strongholds that surround the natural cosmos; the answer reveals that as truth ascends, it becomes rays which pass inward through gates opened in each firmament — four firmaments corresponding to the four quarters of the natural mind — until a gathering agent draws the light together with the small remnant of good still embedded in matter, separates the choicer affections to bear them upward to the celestial register, while the residual portion is returned to the lower natural plane. It is a teaching about the mechanics of redemption: how good imprisoned in externals is sifted, raised through degrees, and reunited with its source.
